title: Driveways
shortDesc: New and replacement driveways for homes and light-commercial lots.
fullDesc: {{name}} forms and pours driveways in {{city}} and {{region}}. Scope, thickness, and base are on the written estimate.
heading: A driveway poured to the written scope
body: The estimate names the thickness and the base for that driveway. Those details stay on the estimate so they can match the lot, not a slogan.

faq.q: Can you replace a driveway that is already cracked?
faq.a: Yes. We look at the slab and the base under it, then quote repair or replacement.

title: Driveway approaches
shortDesc: The approach between the street and the driveway, formed for the traffic it actually takes.
fullDesc: {{name}} replaces and pours driveway approaches in {{region}}. The apron sees street traffic the rest of the drive may not.
heading: The approach is its own pour
body: An approach often carries heavier loads than the rest of the driveway. Thickness for that section is called out on the estimate.

faq.q: Is the approach included with a driveway?
faq.a: Only when the estimate says so. Ask us to price it if the apron is failing with the drive.

title: Patios
shortDesc: Patio slabs sized to the yard, with joints and finish called out before the pour.
fullDesc: {{name}} pours patios in {{city}} for outdoor living space, not as an afterthought on a driveway ticket.
heading: A patio that sheds water
body: We set slope, joints, and finish in the scope so the slab drains away from the building.

faq.q: Do you remove an old patio first?
faq.a: When the estimate includes replacement, removal and haul-off are part of that scope.

title: Sidewalks
shortDesc: Walks from the street, along the house, and between buildings.
fullDesc: {{name}} pours and replaces sidewalks in {{region}}, including sections that have heaved or settled.
heading: Walks you can replace in sections
body: A failed panel does not always mean the whole walk. The estimate says whether we replace a section or the run.

faq.q: Can you match an existing sidewalk?
faq.a: We match width and joint spacing as closely as the site allows. Color and finish are noted on the estimate.

title: Flatwork
shortDesc: Pads, stoops, and other flat slabs that are not a driveway or patio.
fullDesc: {{name}} pours residential and light-commercial flatwork in {{city}} and {{region}}.
heading: Flatwork beyond the driveway
body: Equipment pads, stoops, and similar slabs use the same written scope: thickness, base, and finish.

faq.q: Do you take small pads as well as driveways?
faq.a: Yes. Tell us the size on the form and we will say whether it fits the schedule.

title: Garage slabs
shortDesc: Garage floors for new buildings and replacements inside existing garages.
fullDesc: {{name}} pours garage slabs in {{region}}, including replacements where the old floor has failed.
heading: A garage floor with a written thickness
body: Inside an existing garage, access and demolition are part of the conversation before anyone prices the pour.

faq.q: Can you replace a slab inside a standing garage?
faq.a: Often, yes. We need to see clearance, the door, and what is under the old floor.

title: Repair and replacement
shortDesc: Repair when the slab can be saved, replacement when the base or the concrete has failed.
fullDesc: {{name}} repairs and replaces concrete in {{city}}. We say which one on the estimate after we see the slab.
heading: Repair is not always the right fix
body: Surface damage and a failed base are different jobs. We write the one the site needs.

faq.q: Will a patch fix a sinking slab?
faq.a: A patch covers a surface. Settlement usually means the section, and sometimes the base, has to come out.
